subject.title: Browser backend plugin interface (support third-party drivers via MCP/custom adapter)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a generic third-party browser backend Plugin SDK/registry seam, or keep browser backends limited to first-party/narrow drivers for now?
rationale: The requested seam is both public API and a browser-control security boundary, so automation cannot safely choose the long-term contract by widening driver enums or landing one more built-in adapter.

options.title: Design Generic SDK Registry
options.body: Add a versioned backend contract, registry-owned driver ids, config/schema/client/runtime routing, docs, and security tests before accepting third-party adapters.

options.title: Keep Narrow First-Party Drivers
options.body: Continue handling Browserbase, extension relay, and My Browser needs as individual built-in or bundled-plugin drivers without exposing a generic third-party backend contract yet.

options.title: Defer Until Demand PRs Settle
options.body: Keep this issue open while the Browserbase, My Browser, relay, and sandbox-backend work clarifies the smallest safe registration API.

recommendation.title: Design Generic SDK Registry
recommendation.body: Add a versioned backend contract, registry-owned driver ids, config/schema/client/runtime routing, docs, and security tests before accepting third-party adapters.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the newest first-party extension-driver implementation and has already scoped this issue as a browser backend Plugin SDK design gap.
